close_reason: PR #133 now treats prospective WAL lag crossing as an epoch-fatal safety fuse, not retryable per-push backpressure. Shale returns a structured {:recovery_required, {:wal_limit_exceeded, details}} error, emits error-severity telemetry, preserves any fsynced prefix, and releases every queued successor. Commit finalization promotes the signal and the commit proxy explicitly stops so the Director monitor initiates coordinated recovery; application callers are released as aborted. Docs and tests cover direct/enqueue/drain crossings, multi-successor release, nil posture, telemetry, and commit-proxy termination. Commit 23d71aac; full local suite and remote CI green.
description:
Review finding from worktree-qzr2-wal-trim.

Problem:
Shale checks reject_pushes_above_lag_us once against the current last_version before Pushing. Future pushes can queue while last_version remains below the threshold. When the missing predecessor arrives, do_pending_pushes drains the entire queue without rechecking the prospective lag, advancing and growing the WAL arbitrarily beyond the configured hard limit.

Impact:
The advertised bounded-growth mode does not actually bound a burst containing gaps or concurrent out-of-order delivery.

Acceptance criteria:
- Backpressure is enforced against each transaction's prospective commit version, including entries drained from pending_pushes.
- A queued caller receives a clear error if its transaction cannot be admitted.
- Queue draining leaves ordering state consistent and does not strand callers after rejection.
- Tests enqueue a suffix beyond the limit, fill the gap, and prove the configured bound cannot be crossed.
- Existing unbounded-with-alerting behavior remains unchanged when the hard limit is nil.

comments.text: Reopened for PR #133 review change: WAL limit crossing is not ordinary per-push backpressure after version assignment/resolution. Make it an explicit, loud recovery-required epoch failure; release queued callers; prove commit-proxy fail-fast/recovery signaling in tests.

title: Enforce WAL backpressure while draining queued future pushes
